clue.text: Record award announced for industry

parts.note: to record data is to enter it, in a log or ledger

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the award word is given by how it is said rather than spelt

parts.note: an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A record-breaking prize is publicised for some business sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' signals a word said aloud: the spelling the grid needs ends -ISE, not the -IZE of the prize itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise means business activity or a company, which is what industry also names.

clue.text: Novel item manager wraps

indicators.note: the two words item manager wrap round, and so contain, the letters needed across the word break

explanation.surface: A manager is wrapping up some new object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for 'item' but names the Jane Austen book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen.

clue.text: Try one alternative to bus?

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to tax it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A suggestion that you give some other transport a go instead of the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is one way of getting about instead of catching a bus; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: One protesting about vehicle parked round new arts complex

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning

indicators.note: round says the vehicle word is placed all around the other pieces

parts.note: a motor is a car, a vehicle

indicators.note: complex here means intricate or mixed up, so the letters of arts are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A demonstrator complains about a car left outside a new arts centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a noun (an arts complex) but is the anagram signal; 'round' puts the shuffled letters with N inside the vehicle. 'parked' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who remonstrates objects forcefully, i.e. protests.

clue.text: Takes a spin in posh car?

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a drive in a luxury motor.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin over and over is to roll; a Rolls-Royce is the classic luxury car, often just called a Rolls.

clue.text: Sailor in port for naval engagement

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the port name

parts.note: Seattle is a port city in Washington state
AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman ashore in a harbour town is caught up in a fight at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a battle, and a naval one is fought at sea.

clue.text: Reptile caught by giant bird

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A reptile is snatched up by a huge bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the short form of crocodile, a large reptile.

clue.text: Workers in diamond mines given sponges?

explanation.surface: Miners digging for diamonds are handed sponges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. Some marine sponges bore into rock, as miners bore through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners drilling through rock bore it; certain sponges also burrow into stone and shell.

clue.text: Challenging college about examination process

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
testing is the process of examining

explanation.surface: A college is disputing how its exams are run.
explanation.definitionFit: Contesting a claim means disputing or challenging it.

clue.text: Former ruler saw one secure in retirement

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in retirement means going back, so the word for secure is read backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it

explanation.surface: An old monarch saw one person safely set up after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a verb but is a noun for a proverb. 'in retirement' turns NAIL into LIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximilian was the name of Holy Roman Emperors and of the Habsburg emperor of Mexico, all past monarchs.

clue.text: Read article on science

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the article follows the science abbreviation

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone peruses a piece about science.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a text is to look over or read it.

clue.text: The Gay Gordons, for example, turned out melodic at end

indicators.note: turned out suggests something made over into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance ended up tuneful at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gay Gordons is a traditional Scottish ballroom dance; the twelve letters of 'melodic at end' rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gay Gordons is a traditional sequence dance of the kind called old-fashioned ballroom, an instance of the type.

clue.text: Powerless to keep a small boat safe from attack

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the powerless word contains the other pieces

parts.note: unable means powerless to do something
a sail is a sailing vessel, a boat

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the strength to hold on to a dinghy that is secure against assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' suggests protecting the boat, but it means holding the pieces inside the word for powerless, which is split around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassailable means impossible to attack or defeat, invulnerable.

clue.text: Injured toes? After operation at hospital, you'll begin manipulative treatment

indicators.note: injured means damaged or hurt, so the letters of toes are knocked out of order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: begin says only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Hurt toes? After surgery in hospital, you'll be starting physio-style therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges TOES into OSTE; 'begin' takes Y from 'you'll'. 'manipulative' sounds sinister but means hands-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy treats the body by manipulating bones and muscles by hand.

clue.text: Late-flowering plant wife put in ground finally grew

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy
to inter is to bury, putting in the ground
rose means grew or increased

explanation.surface: A plant flowering late grew at last after the wife bedded it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' is part of the surface picture and acts only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter rose, or hellebore, blooms in the cold months when most plants have finished.

clue.text: Worshipper abroad thus is accepting advice by theologian, principally

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for thus holds the word for advice

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a hint is a piece of advice or tip

indicators.note: principally means first or chiefly, picking the opening letter of theologian

explanation.surface: A foreign worshipper takes counsel from a leading theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' belongs to the definition: Shinto is the native religion of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Shinto, the Japanese religion, worships in a faith foreign to Britain.

clue.text: Like 20 during church ceremony

parts.note: in means during, as in in the morning
a service is a ceremony of worship in church

explanation.surface: Something happening while a church ceremony is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is PARLOURMAIDS: domestic servants were said to be 'in service'.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaids and parlourmaids working in a household were described as being employed as domestic servants.

clue.text: Cards — ace and king-held by youngster

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the youngster word goes around the ace and king letters

parts.note: a tot is a small child
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
R, for Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A child grips an ace and a king in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a pack of picture cards used in fortune-telling and some games.

clue.text: Bit part actor in old pictures making comeback

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: making comeback means returning, so the word for pictures is read backwards

parts.note: art is pictures and other works

explanation.surface: A minor player from old films returns to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old pictures' looks like old films; it is EX plus ART, the latter turned to TRA by 'making comeback'.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer with a tiny non-speaking role in a film crowd.

clue.text: It removes creases from man's tie or pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, poor, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something smooths the wrinkles out of a man's necktie or trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is the anagram signal (British slang for 'rubbish').
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron presses clothes flat, smoothing away wrinkles with heat and moisture.

clue.text: Domestic staff giving marines help in dangerous environment

indicators.note: environment here means surroundings, so the dangerous word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: parlous means perilous or dangerous
RM stands for Royal Marines
aid means help

explanation.surface: Household servants are getting assistance from marines amid peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is the container signal: the word for dangerous wraps round the marines and the help, and 'giving' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlourmaids were servants who waited at table and kept the reception rooms of a large house.

clue.text: A Northerner's tie, of course

parts.note: a Scot comes from Scotland, the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's necktie, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' doubles as a nod to Ascot racecourse, the English horse-racing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad cravat-style neckcloth.

clue.text: Brave victims of hunter

explanation.surface: Courageous prey of the chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means willing or plucky; game is also animals shot for sport.

clue.text: Film star with old-fashioned sex appeal appearing in small part

indicators.note: appearing in means set within, so the sex appeal word goes inside the part abbreviation

parts.note: PT is the short form of part
it was a 1920s word for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: An actor with retro allure turns up in a bit role.
explanation.definitionFit: Brad Pitt is a Hollywood actor.

clue.text: Maybe saw stolen goods being put back

indicators.note: being put back means returned, so the word for stolen goods is read backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder, stolen goods

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone saw the stolen items being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' reads as a verb but is the noun, an example of an implement, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of an implement.

clue.text: Report of wrongdoings by people, on leaving US city

indicators.note: report of means a spoken account, so how the sins are said gives the letters

parts.note: wrongdoings are sins, and a pair of them gives the said word

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the word for on is taken out of the word for people

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An account of crimes by people as they go out of an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' says SIN SIN aloud as CINCIN; 'on leaving' removes ON from NATION to leave NATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cincinnati is a large city in Ohio.

clue.text: Frenchman in natty vest

indicators.note: in says the letters are contained within the words natty vest

explanation.surface: A Gallic man wearing a smart waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French man's name, as in Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Resolution of dispute in the community

explanation.surface: A dispute in a neighbourhood is resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is an agreement ending a quarrel, and also a small colony or village where people live.
